title: Route every train a browser spec covers from an interlocking

facts.note: browser_spec = a *.e2e.ts file run by Playwright, OR any test file of any name or extension whose header comments carry a journey marker (// Train:, // Journey:, // URN: test:train:…, // URN: test:journey:…). Two independent branches: (a) *.e2e.ts name AND run by Playwright (needs Playwright config/runner inspection); (b) qualifying header marker (needs header-comment parsing). A *.e2e.ts name alone, without Playwright running it and without a header marker, does not qualify.

Non-exhaustive and insufficient by itself: a *.e2e.ts match is a browser spec only if the file is also run by Playwright. Independently, any test file with a qualifying header journey marker is in scope regardless of name. Vendored/generated trees (node_modules, dist, build, _generated) excluded.

Requires cross-referencing the declared train a spec binds to against the selectors of all interlocking routes (htmx_e2e_detector). Evaluated over the whole repository state, so existing unchanged violations are reported too, not only diff-introduced ones.

fires: A *.e2e.ts file run by Playwright declares // Train: <declared train> and no interlocking route selects that train.
A misnamed test file of any name or extension (not *.e2e.ts) carries a // URN: test:train:… header marker binding to a declared train that no interlocking route selects.
An existing, unchanged browser spec binds to a declared train that no interlocking route selects.
An interlocking route is removed or changed so that a train still covered by a browser spec is no longer selected by any route.
doesNotFire: A browser spec binds to a declared train that at least one interlocking route selects.
A unit test merely mentions a journey URN inside a string literal, without a header journey marker.
A *.e2e.ts file that is not run by Playwright and has no qualifying header journey marker.
The spec lives under node_modules, dist, build or _generated.
The spec binds to an undeclared train (reported by tester.htmx.e2e-binds-declared-subject instead).

given: A browser spec exists in the repository: a *.e2e.ts file run by Playwright, or any test file (any name) whose header comments carry a journey marker (// Train:, // Journey:, // URN: test:train:…, // URN: test:journey:…)
when: the spec binds to a declared train
then: That declared train MUST be selected by at least one interlocking route.
prefer: Route the train from an interlocking so the application can actually reach it.
Or rebind the spec to a train that an interlocking route already selects.
avoid: Keeping a spec green against a train nothing in the application can reach.
Renaming a browser spec away from *.e2e.ts to dodge the check; header journey markers still classify it.
unless: The spec is in a vendored or generated tree (node_modules, dist, build, _generated) — never scanned.
The bound train is undeclared — that is reported by tester.htmx.e2e-binds-declared-subject, not here.
why: A spec can stay green while exercising a train nothing in the application can reach; covering an unrouted train proves nothing about the product.
evidence: For every browser spec (existing or new), the declared train it binds to is listed as selected by at least one interlocking route.
htmx_e2e_detector reports no covered-but-unrouted train findings.
verifier_detail: browser_spec = a *.e2e.ts file run by Playwright, or any test file whose header comments carry a journey marker (// Train:, // Journey:, // URN: test:train:…, // URN: test:journey:…), so a misnamed one is still judged. A *.e2e.ts name without Playwright running it and without a header marker does not qualify.
A unit test that merely mentions a journey URN in a string is not a browser_spec.
Never scan vendored and generated trees: node_modules, dist, build, _generated.
Only declared trains are judged; undeclared trains are reported by tester.htmx.e2e-binds-declared-subject.
